source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 18 assumes positivity Pr(X)>0 for each treatment variable and gives an F-identifiability iff reduction; its proof merges an auxiliary root with an observed parent into a Cartesian-product state.
Theorem 6.1 states that when IDENTIFY+ returns a positivity condition and identifying formula, they are correct.
Proposition 4 characterizes identifiability through an invariant cut; the paper says complete invariant-cut discovery is beyond its scope outside the classical strict-positivity case.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 8, Theorem 1; pp. 1 and 7–8, abstract and polynomial-program construction
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reduces discrete causal bounding to polynomial programming and proves its optimization yields sharp bounds, including point identification when the range collapses.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient graphical condition and an algorithm for identifiable joint interventions in recursive semi-Markovian models.
The paper proves CSI nonidentifiability is NP-hard and presents a sound automated CSI-aware identification calculus.
The paper gives a sound and complete procedure only when CSI relations are limited to observed parentless control nodes.
The paper gives finite canonical discrete SCM representations and translates counterfactual bounding into polynomial programming.
DML-ID constructs influence-function-based estimators for identifiable causal functionals and establishes debiasing and double-robustness properties.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Specify a finite benchmark family where Chen--Darwiche reduction or Hwang-style guarded search fails to supply the required original-alphabet certificate, then require F-ID+ to return a worked success and a worked algebraic separator with its stated size bound.

Promote the algorithmic distinction into a quantified theorem target: give the input encoding, certificate-verification complexity, and a strict asymptotic or operational advantage over generic real quantifier elimination on a named family.

Add a non-toy family extending the binary rectangle in which a symbolic vector region remains closed form or admits a provably smaller guarded representation than the corresponding polynomial program.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the fixed-alphabet guarded-dichotomy kernel, retaining the binary and inference statements as validation rungs rather than headline novelty claims.
